alex: Heads up — after #4827 merged the arch-capability sweep is toggling BF16 benchmarks differently and I'm seeing a perf regression on short sequences (8-32). cc @mira

mira: Huh, saw an odd spike in the smoke tests earlier but didn't trace it. Is this on the canary infra or prod canary? :eyes:

alex: Canaries. Quick paste from the profiler: 
```
[run] model=redwood-13b
sequence=8 (chat)
kernel picked: matmul_tc_v2 (tensor-core path)
SM reported: 7.0
flags: tensor_cores=enabled, bf16_hw=true, fp8=false
latency p50: 11.9ms -> 18.4ms (after probe)
KV cache path: kv-interleaved -> kv-blocked (autopick)
```

jonah: Wait, our autotuner policy currently does: if sm_major >= 7 && tensor_cores_detected -> prefer tc kernels. That heuristic is simple but doesn't consider seq length or batch size. For tiny seqs tc kernel setup overhead can dominate.

mira: Exactly. The kernel selection logic assumed larger GEMM sizes where TC helps. We need a sequence-length heuristic: prefer tc only when estimated GEMM dims > threshold.

alex: Repro steps I used: `./tools/profiler --model redwood-13b --seq 8 --batch 1 --device canary-a --kernel-logs` 
Output for the kernel pick is in the canary logs under `kernel.pick.v2` on shard 3.

sarah: Is KV cache behavior related? I see the autotuner also switched to kv-blocked on that run which changes memory layout and tensor shapes. Might be compounding the regression.

jonah: Good catch. kv-blocked gives bigger matmul dims for attention compute which should favor TC, but for seq 8 the overhead of reorganizing KV can be bigger than compute wins. We have two competing heuristics firing: kv layout -> tc kernel.

alex: I attached a minimal repro script in the canary workspace that toggles `FORCE_KERNELOPTIONS` to force non-tc kernel. Forcing non-tc drops p50 back to ~12ms. So it's definitely the kernel path.

mira: Can we add a cheap cost-model check in the selector: compute_estimated_flops = B * S * D; if flops < X then avoid tc despite SM flags? Even a simple threshold would prevent this.

jonah: Yep. Proposal: add sequence-length aware threshold and a KV-layout penalty term. Rough pseudo: 
```
score_tc = perf_model.tc_latency( dims ) + kv_penalty(layout)
score_native = perf_model.native_latency( dims )
choose argmin(score_*)
```
We can bootstrap perf_model from microbenchmarks we already run per-arch.

perf-bot: nightly.autotune: ran microbench for sm=7.0 yesterday; tc_vs_native matrix uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/matrix/7.0.csv

mira: Perfect — can pull that matrix and derive a rough threshold. I'll sketch the selector change and a quick unit test.

sarah: For safety, add a canary gating rule: unless the new selector increases p50 by >2x on short seqs, roll forward; else auto-revert. Also log selection reasons to tracing: `kernel_reason` tag.

alex: Agreed. Also need to ensure backward compatibility with FP8/BF16 flags: the probe sometimes reports `bf16_hw=true` but on runtimes where BF16 is emulated latency differs. We should surface `bf16_mode` (hw|emu) not just boolean.

jonah: Oh nice — that explains some of the noise. Current probe only reports `bf16_supported` without mode. I'll update the probe to return `bf16_mode=hw|emu|none`.

mira: Timeline: I'll open a small PR with selector logic + test. Jonah updates probe. Alex will run canary with forced non-tc and provide perf traces. Sarah will add canary gating rule in rollout config.

alex: Running forced-non-tc now and uploading traces to `s3://redwood-canary/traces/1796008000/`. Initial diff: p50 18.4ms -> 12.1ms. KV layout alone accounts for ~1.2ms; kernel path is ~5ms.

perf-bot: compare: s3://redwood-canary/traces/1796008000/forced-non-tc.log vs baseline -> p50 delta -6.3ms.

sarah: I'll hold the canary rollback rule open until PR lands. If we flip selector we should also add a quick perf test as part of CI to catch regressions on seq <= 32.

jonah: Also considering adding a cheap runtime check: if measured p50 after switching to tc is > threshold for first N requests, fallback to native kernel for that model/version. Kind of a runtime self-heal.

mira: Good idea. Fallback policy could be per-model and per-route. We'll need to record counts to avoid flip-flop.

alex: Thanks team. I'll leave the canary paused and update thread with the traces link once uploaded.

infra-bot: deploy: rollback executed for canary group `canary-a` to commit `abc123def` at 14:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

mira: Thanks — I'll land the selector PR this afternoon and include the `bf16_mode` probe change in the same CL to reduce churn.

jonah: After that, let's schedule a microbenchmark run across SM 6.x-8.x with varying seqs (4,8,16,32,64) and kv layouts to derive a robust threshold table.

sarah: I'll create the perf-suite ticket and CI job. Ticket: PERF-1328.

alex: Great. Marking this thread resolved for now. :thumbsup:
